extraction.Name: Paddy Star
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not want the patent and protested against taking it but did not know that he could return it
extraction.Recorded patent: the patent was held until March 31st, 1920 when affiant had it recorded
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: Mortgaged and sold; land was foreclosed on and lost by foreclosure
extraction.Buyer: land was sold to J. B. Campbell of Interior, South Dakota
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: the mortgage was foreclosed because affiant could not pay the interest and taxes on the land; land was really sold because affiant could not pay the taxes on it and the mortgage for $600.00
extraction.Occupation/Income: cannot work at all and is dependent on his wife for his living; has no means whatsoever upon which to live and has no horses or cattle or other personal property or land
extraction.NOTES: Allotment on Pine Ridge reservation for Section 29, Twp. 41 N.R. 38 W., 6th P.M., Washabaugh County, South Dakota; patent was for North half of said section; patent was sent by registered mail and affiant signed a registry receipt; borrowed $600.00 from a bank in Wagner, S.D. and gave a mortgage on the land; land sold in Fall of 1920 to J.B. Campbell; all affiant received was a second mortgage on Mellette County property which was subject to a first mortgage, first mortgage being foreclosed; only consideration received was the sum of $600.00 originally borrowed; in fair condition mentally, in very poor condition of health; lives with his wife and is wholly dependent on her; neither the Government, the State nor County has contributed to his support since the patent was issued; no one dependent on him for support; land at time of sale was worth $20.00 per acre; affiant was not really defrauded out of his land but if he had known he did not have to take the patent and that the land was not really assessable he would still have it; the $600 borrowed was not used to pay a prior debt; affiant does not remember having the terms of the second mortgage explained to him; document received JAN 11 1929, No. 1070
